name: Venus Flytrap
summary: The Venus flytrap is the accepted species Dionaea muscipula, a perennial carnivorous plant native to the Carolinas. North Carolina Extension lists both seed and division propagation.

identity.guidance: Kew accepts Dionaea muscipula J.Ellis and places it in Droseraceae. The common name Venus flytrap refers to this species here; no named cultivar is implied.

cultivation.short: Use the cited wet, acidic growing context
cultivation.guidance: North Carolina Extension describes full sun or partial shade and persistently moist to occasionally wet, acidic soil. These are outdoor/site conditions, not a hydroponic nutrient recipe or a household watering schedule.

propagation.guidance: North Carolina Extension lists seed and division as propagation strategies. The source does not specify a home seed-sowing protocol, germination timing, or cultivar fidelity; those details remain unresolved.

problems.short: Avoid treating carnivory as a fertilizer requirement
problems.guidance: The cited profile places this species in nutrient-poor acidic wetland conditions. It does not provide a container fertilizer or hydroponic feeding schedule, so none is inferred here.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: Wetland ecology does not establish suitability for recirculating hydroponic nutrient solutions.

evidence.note: NC State Extension describes the species as clumping.
NC State's 6–12 inch range is converted to centimeters; source scope is species.
NC State's 6–8 inch range is converted to centimeters; source scope is species.
NC State Extension lists full sun and partial shade for outdoor cultivation; the profile reports the supported full-sun category only because v1 does not express partial shade separately.

name: Cape Sundew
summary: Cape sundew is the accepted perennial species Drosera capensis. The South African National Biodiversity Institute documents moist acidic cultivation and propagation from fresh surface-sown seed or vegetative cuttings.

identity.guidance: Kew accepts Drosera capensis L. and identifies its native range in the South African Cape. The public identity is species-level, not a color-form cultivar.

cultivation.short: Keep the growing medium continuously moist
cultivation.guidance: SANBI's PlantZAfrica describes moist conditions and full sun to semi-shade outdoors. Its botanical-garden cultivation notes are retained in context; they do not establish a hydroponic recipe.

propagation.short: Fresh seed and cuttings are documented
propagation.guidance: SANBI describes sowing fresh seed on the surface of moist growing medium without covering it, and also documents leaf or root cuttings. Seed guidance is species-level; no numeric germination duration or temperature is supplied.

problems.guidance: SANBI notes that drying can cause drooping and reduced mucilage production. This symptom is not by itself a diagnosis of the cause; assess moisture and growing conditions before intervention.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: Carnivorous-plant wet-media guidance does not establish suitability for conventional hydroponic nutrient solutions.

growthHabits.reason: The selected institutional source does not establish a controlled growth-habit value.

height.reason: No dimensions are asserted from the reviewed selected source set.

spread.reason: No dimensions are asserted from the reviewed selected source set.

evidence.note: SANBI lists full sun to semi-shade outdoors; only its explicit full-sun category is carried because v1 does not separately represent partial shade.

name: Pinguicula primuliflora
summary: Pinguicula primuliflora is an accepted southeastern U.S. carnivorous perennial. Its leaf-tip plantlets make vegetative propagation a documented, practical route; cultivation notes are attributed to a specialist source.

identity.guidance: Kew accepts Pinguicula primuliflora C.E.Wood & R.K.Godfrey, in Lentibulariaceae. The common name butterwort is broader than this species and is kept as a search alias, not a replacement identity.

cultivation.short: Moist medium and filtered light in the cited specialist account
cultivation.guidance: The specialist species account describes moist, aerated growing medium and indirect or filtered light, with caution against direct sun in its stated habitat context. It is a specialist cultivation account, not an institutional hydroponic recommendation.

propagation.short: Leaf-tip plantlets are the documented practical route
propagation.guidance: The specialist account describes numerous plantlets forming at leaf tips and rooting before separation. Seed formation is noted as occasional in the described clone, so seed propagation is not presented as a dependable routine method for this identity.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: A moist carnivorous-plant medium is not evidence of hydroponic nutrient-solution compatibility.

growthHabits.reason: The selected sources do not map habit to the controlled profile vocabulary.

light.reason: Specialist light wording was not forced into the current outdoor exposure categories.

name: Nepenthes × ventrata
variety: Horticultural hybrid identity; no named cultivar specified
summary: Nepenthes × ventrata is documented by Singapore NParks as a hybrid of N. alata and N. ventricosa. NParks reports tissue-culture propagation and a moist, low-nutrient medium; those details do not establish seed or hydroponic protocols.

identity.short: Hybrid identity, not a species or cultivar claim
identity.guidance: NParks identifies Nepenthes × ventrata as a natural hybrid between N. alata and N. ventricosa. This record preserves the horticultural hybrid name and does not treat it as a named cultivar or as either parent species.

cultivation.short: Moist, low-nutrient, well-drained medium in NParks guidance
cultivation.guidance: NParks describes moist but well-drained, low-nutrient media and semi-shade. These are horticultural-medium conditions for this hybrid; they are not converted into recirculating hydroponics, EC, or pH values.

propagation.short: Tissue culture is the documented commercial propagation route
propagation.guidance: NParks reports that this hybrid has been widely propagated by tissue culture. This does not establish that seed is impossible; a reliable seed protocol and seed fidelity for the marketed hybrid remain unverified.

hydroponicSuitability.reason: Moist, low-nutrient substrate guidance does not support hydroponic system compatibility.

growthHabits.reason: No controlled growth-habit value is asserted from the reviewed source.

height.reason: No dimensions established for the hybrid in the selected source.

spread.reason: No dimensions established for the hybrid in the selected source.

light.reason: NParks' semi-shade wording is not mapped to an unsupported indoor-light or outdoor-exposure value.
